'''Moses Chan Hung-Wai''' ({{zh|t=陳鴻渭|p=Chén Hóngwèi}}) is a Chinese-American physicist who is Evan Pugh Professor at [[Pennsylvania State University]]. He was a postdoctoral associate at [[Duke University]] and has been a professor at [[Penn State University Park]] since 1979.

Through the years, Chan's work has spanned many diverse topics.<ref>[http://www.phys.psu.edu/people/display/index.html?person_id=21&mode=research&submode=publications Complete list of publications.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060906050913/http://www.phys.psu.edu/people/display/index.html?person_id=21&mode=research&submode=publications |date=6 September 2006 }}</ref> For his numerous contributions to low-temperature physics, in 1996 he shared the prestigious [[Fritz London]] Memorial prize with [[Carl Wieman]] and [[Eric A. Cornell]].<ref>[http://www.phy.duke.edu/~hm/flondonprizeawards.html Fritz London Memorial Prize<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> He was elected a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences |National Academy of Sciences]] in 2000, and a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2004.<ref>[https://www.amacad.org/multimedia/pdfs/classlist.pdf List of active members by class, October 24, 2014]</ref>

Chan is known for the experimental discovery of evidence for a new [[supersolid]] [[quantum]] state of matter,<ref>{{cite journal |author=[[Eun-Seong Kim |E. Kim]] and M. H. W. Chan |title=Probable Observation of a Supersolid Helium Phase | journal=Nature |volume=427 |issue=6971 |year=2004 |pages=225–227 |pmid=14724632 |doi=10.1038/nature02220|bibcode = 2004Natur.427..225K | s2cid=3112651 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.nature.com/nsu/040112/040112-7.html ''Nature'' story on a supersolid experiment]</ref> predicted theoretically in 1969 by Alexander Andreev and Ilya Liftshitz, and its subsequent refutation.<ref>{{cite journal |author=D. Y. Kim and M. H. W. Chan |title=Absence of Supersolidity in Solid Helium in Porous Vycor Glass |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=109 |issue=15 |year=2012 |article-number=155301 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.109.155301|arxiv = 1207.7050 |bibcode = 2012PhRvL.109o5301K |pmid=23102323|s2cid=23590787 }}</ref>  Other significant discoveries include the experimental observation of Critical Casimir effect<ref>{{cite journal | author=R. Garcia and M. H. W. Chan |title=Critical Fluctuation-Induced Thinning of 4He Films near the Superfluid Transition |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=83 |issue=6 |pages=1187–1190 |year=1999 |bibcode=1999PhRvL..83.1187G |doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.83.1187 | s2cid=51372560 }}</ref> and the experimental confirmation of 2D [[Ising model]].<ref>{{cite journal | author=H. K. Kim and M. H. W. Chan | title=An Experimental Determination of a Two-Dimensional Liquid-Vapor Critical Point Exponent| journal=Physical Review Letters | volume=53 | issue=2| pages=170–173 | year=1984|bibcode = 1984PhRvL..53..170K |doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.170 }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Born in Xi'an in 1946, he moved to [[Hong Kong]] in his childhood and completed his primary and secondary education in [[Yuen Long]] District.<ref>{{cite news |title=土產物理學家盼多撥資源發展科學 |url=http://std.stheadline.com/archive/fullstory.asp?andor=or&year1=2005&month1=7&day1=1&year2=2005&month2=12&day2=9&category=g&id=20051108g02&keyword1=&keyword2= |access-date=5 January 2019 |work=星島日報 |date=1 July 2005 |archive-date=9 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190609094757/http://std.stheadline.com/archive/fullstory.asp?andor=or&year1=2005&month1=7&day1=1&year2=2005&month2=12&day2=9&category=g&id=20051108g02&keyword1=&keyword2= |url-status=live }}</ref> In 1967, Chan received his bachelor's degree from [[Bridgewater College]] in Virginia, United States. From 1969 to 1970, he taught at the [[University of Hong Kong]]. In 1974, he received his doctorate from [[Cornell University]]. From 1973 to 1976, he conducted postdoctoral research at Duke University. From 1976 to 1979, Chen taught at the [[University of Toledo]]. In 1979, he joined Pennsylvania State University.<ref name="physics.sjtu">{{cite web |title=Single-fluxon controlled Resistance Switching in a Nanowire |url=http://www.physics.sjtu.edu.cn/node/1294 |website=Colloquium |publisher=上海交通大学物理与天文学院 |access-date=5 January 2019 |archive-date=29 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190629161854/https://www.physics.sjtu.edu.cn/node/1294 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Honors ==
He received the [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1986 and the Fritz London Memorial Prize in 1996. He was elected a Fellow of the American Physical Society in 1987, a member of the National Academy of Sciences in 2000, a member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences in 2004, and a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science in 2007.<ref name="physics.sjtu" />
